newsitem.title: FINLAND: WEEK AHEAD - FINNISH MARKETS TO FOCUS MAINLY ON US.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - FINNISH MARKETS TO FOCUS MAINLY ON US.

text.p: Finnish financial markets are expected to focus mainly on events on international markets for direction next week.
The EU's finance minister meeting (ECOFIN) on Monday and Thursday's Bundesbank council meeting will be closely watched.
At home, October trade balance and current account estimates due for release by the Bank of Finland on Wednesday and Thursday's state treasury auction of the 10.00 percent 2001 bond will be in focus.
All markets will be closed December 6 for Independence Day.
U.S. INDICATORS
U.S. economic indicators in the spotlight are November payrolls and unemployment, due on Friday, as well as NAPM and October leading indicators, due on Monday, analysts said.
"A rate hike (in the U.S.) is expected to take place not earlier than next year," said Juha Lehtonen, analyst at Merita Bank.
He noted that the U.S. economic indicators will be important guidelines for markets in Europe even though German bunds seemed to some extent to be living a life of their own.
Reuters consensus forecast for U.S. November payrolls is +160,000 compared to +210,000 in October, with unemployment seen unchanged at 5.2 percent. The figures will be published at 1530/1330 GMT.
ECOFIN, BUNDESBANK MEETINGS
EU finance ministers meet in Brussels on Monday. The provisional agenda includes European Investment Bank loans to third countries and taxation issues.
But analysts expect that they will also discuss the EMU budget stability pact, even though no final decisions are seen before the Dublin summit in December.
The Bundesbank will hold its regular council meeting on Thursday; no changes are expected in key German interest rates, analysts said.
FINNISH C/A SEEN IN SURPLUS
The Bank of Finland's estimates for the October current account (C/A) and trade balance figures are due on Wednesday around 0900/0700 GMT.
Merita Bank forecasts a 3.5 billion markka trade surplus and its C/A surplus forecast is 1.7 billion markka. Danish Unibank's forecasts are 3.3 billion and 2.0 billion respectively.
"(C/A and trade balance) figures are not expected to have any impact ... unless they markedly differ from recent figures," said Ari Aaltonen, chief economist at Postipankki.
The central bank's September trade surplus estimate was 3.7 billion markka, and the derived C/A surplus estimate was 2.3 billion.
GOOD DEMAND SEEN FOR 2001 BOND, T-BILLS
The State Treasury Office (STO) will auction up to 1.5 billion markka of the 10.00 percent 2001 bond on Thursday.
"I think the auctioned amount will be close to that unless some turmoil emerges on the market," Lehtonen at Merita said.
The outstanding amount of the 2001-paper is 27.1 billion markka.
Lehtonen also expected the STO to raise around 1.5 billion markka -- the treasury's own target amount -- in the regular weekly auction of treasury bill on Tuesday.
The STO will be issuing 99-day and 344-day T-bills.
LITTLE INTEREST IN MONEY SUPPLY
The Bank of Finland will release October money aggregate and lending data on Thursday. These figures are expected to be largely ignored by the markets, analysts said.
Over the past months, the M1 figure has increased, while M2 and M3 aggregates have contracted.
"Part of the assets have been moved to cheque and transactions accounts away from time-linked deposits," said Teijo Rantatupa," market analyst at OKOBANK.

Pentti Pikkarainen, head of the monetary policy department at the Bank of Finland, told Reuters that although the importance of the markka's exchange rate had increased in monetary policy as Finland joined the ERM, the central bank will continue to include money supply and lending figures when forecasting inflation.
"There is no reason to leave them out," he said.
